text_fidelity_a:
Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology I purchased the Igloo BMX Cooler to replace an Ozark Trail 25qt rotomolded cooler that I purchased from Wal-Mart before an impromptu camping trip. I was very disappointed with the OT cooler, it claimed to hold ice for 4.5 days but on day two of my trip over half the ice was melted. I had a family member coming out to visit and camp with me so I decided to order the 52qt version of the Igloo BMX. It was actually cheaper than the Wal-Mart cooler and twice the size.

We filled the Igloo up on a Sunday afternoon packed pretty full with food, beer and water. We were planning on a 3-day trip. I saved as much ice as I could at home and we bought one more bag on the way out of town. Day 1 after over 24 hours I opened the drain and only a tiny bit of water came out. Already much better performance. On Tuesday we moved campsites and got gas and added another bag of ice since we bought more food to replenish. Day 3 on Wednesday a fair amount of water drained from the cooler but it still had plenty of ice and was plenty cold. I had put 8 frozen water bottles inside and they were all frozen still.

I went to empty the cooler on Day 4, a full ~96 hours of use and there was still a lot of ice left in it. I have no doubt that you could make this last 5 days or even longer if you keep adding fresh ice every couple of days. If we didn't add the second bag, most of it would have probably melted by day 3/4.

At the time of this review I purchased the red/black 52qt cooler for $77. I'm impressed enough with it that I decided to order a 25qt one was well for solo trips and returned my Ozark Trail cooler. I will add another review or update this one after I use the 25qt cooler. But $140 for a nice rotomolded 52qt and 25qt cooler is less than half the price of ONE comparable Yeti. So glad I didn't buy into the hype.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology

I still have those gloves and although they are a bit stiff, you'd never know they were used so much as they hardly look worn. Since the Lee Haney gloves are not padded, I decided to try these gloves both because I expected an increase in comfort and as an enticement to get me back into lifting again.

The gloves I received are a size "Large" and they are heavier than any other lifting gloves I've tried before; the pair weighs in at 6.2 ounces according to my dietary food scale. However, you don't notice the weight when wearing them. Below are the pros and cons I noticed during use:

PROS:

1. The gloves are well padded. In fact, the padding is an excellent feature for when I perform lifts where the weight is in the palm of my hand, such as when doing a bench press or incline press or when the weight is evenly distributed throughout the hand such as when doing squats using a [[ASIN:B0000AVAL2 Advanced Fitness Manta Ray]].

2. I usually take a size medium or large in a woman's glove and this size large fit me comfortably.

3. The extra "leather-like" flap that you secure to the fastened wrist wrap offers extra security so that the wrap won't come undone during a lift and the gloves will remain securely fastened.

CONS:

1. The padding on the pinkie finger was uncomfortable for me when doing dead lifts because the bar was evenly distributed through my hand and the padding on the pinkie finger seemed to get in the way. It almost caused a pressure point of discomfort during each entire lift (ascent and descent).

2. The wrist wrap was awkward to fasten because not only did I have to wrap the strap around my wrist, but then I had to flip over the "leather-like" flap and make sure it fastened to the Velcro on the back of the flap.

3. I was bothered by the white tag inside the right glove during lifting. Perhaps the manufacturer could either leave the tags out or put them on the non-Velcro portion of the wrist wrap.

4. I don't like that the two pieces of fabric used to fasten the glove to the cardboard insert it came with remain sewed to the glove. Basically, the gloves arrive with two tags on each glove that fastens to the cardboard packaging. Those tags remain as part of the glove and to me they are annoying as I see no reason to ever use those tags again.

I do think that if men are considering purchasing these gloves, they might want to consider ordering the next size up. My boyfriend always takes a size "Large" in men's gloves and he had to struggle to get these size Large gloves on his hands.

These gloves are thick and although they feel well-made they don't look well-made on close inspection. Therefore, I'm concerned that the stitching on the padding may come loose. When comparing these gloves to my Lee Haney gloves, I doubt they will last as long but only time will tell.

If padding is important, then these gloves offer that and certainly cushion the lifter during many lifts. However, for me I can only give these gloves an average rating because of the cons and my concern that the stitching around the padding will come loose.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves

text_fidelity_a:
CyclingDeal Folding Bike Foldable Bicycle with 7 Speed Shimano Gears 20-inch Aluminium Wheels Easy Folding City Bicycle with Disc Brake, Rear Carry Rack, Front and Rear Fenders I have several folding bikes for use by the family. We swear by them.

Our first folding bike was a Euromini Campo. I bought one, then we purchased one for my wife. Those bikes were a nice low-end introduction to folding bikes with a $200 price point. About a year later I purchased a Dahon Vigor. An excellent bike at a $750 price point. An order of magnitude superior to the Euromini bikes in terms of many components and build and ride quality (one Euromini frame has a crack near the seatpost and we had to replace both bottom brackets after only a year).

This CyclingDeal bike, although a brand unknown to me, provides a level of quality on par with my Dahon Vigor. In terms of features, the CyclingDeal comes with superior brakes (disc), equivalent quality tires/rims and several features the Vigor lacks (fenders, quality rear rack). Other components such as headset, bars and grips are of significantly lower quality. The CyclingDeal shifting, while inferior to the SRAM system of the Dahon, is equivalent to the Euromini Campo, consisting of a 7 Speed Shimano with Revoshifter. The Aluminum frame is MUCH lighter and somewhat stiffer than the Campo and ride quality is closer to that of the Dahon. This is also the lightest adult folding bike I've ever used. About 2 lbs heavier than my son's folding Vilano cuiser (we added a longer seat post, brakes and a sprung saddle). If you have a Campo, you'll notice how much lighter the CyclingDeal is...

If this bike said Dahon on the side, no one would bat an eye. From a distance. A closer inspection of the frame shows a slightly lower weld quality/frame construction as well as low-end consumer detailing ("super easy folding system...")

If you're looking for a first folding bike on Amazon. This should definitely be in the running. You will only need to replace the bar grips with some Ergon GP1s. And maybe the saddle if you weigh more than 200 lbs.

To like: quick release wheels, disc brakes, lightweight frame, fenders, rear rack
To hate: low-end detailing, cheap grips, no magnetic closures on folding system

Recommended!

I'll update this review after 100 miles...
text_fidelity_b: CyclingDeal Folding Bike Foldable Bicycle with 7 Speed Shimano Gears 20-inch Aluminium Wheels Easy Folding City Bicycle with Disc Brake, Rear Carry Rack, Front and Rear Fenders

text_fidelity_a:
1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage The stand holds the bike upright and so it will not fall sideways.
Because it grips the front wheel so that it cannot turn right or left.

Nor slip backwards out.
And as you can see in the picture the bottom of the stand makes the bile roll back uphill,
and so gravity holds the bike from rolling backwards.

I do not agree with those who say this should work to hold a bike in the back of a pickup.
The bike could bounce out (overcome gravity) and roll backwards out.

In the garage, you will want a cover over the bike and stand to keep dust and dirt
out of the parts that have grease (the chain for instance).

Indoors you need a long pad (like an exercise pad to keep the dirty tires off the carpet.

Another (better for cleanliness) is a 'work stand' because these hold the bike in the air
and only the stand touches the floor (like a Park brand work stand). But these take about
15 seconds to load and unload the bike instead of 2 seconds like this Bikehand parking rack.
And work stands are much more expensive.
But a work stand hold bike so that you can do mechanical work on it, thus saving paying
hundreds to a bike shop for repacking bearings and such that you can do yourself with
a work stand and some specialized bike tools.

There are lots of other ways to go too, holders that mount to the wall or ceiling,
some have hoist ropes to raise and lower.

This stand is a very sensible and cheap solution, just keep in mind when the
bike is in a garage, then it needs a cover (cloth or plastic). Amazon sells
lots of these covers, they cost less than this stand.
text_fidelity_b: 1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage

Rhino Laces Unbreakable Shoe Laces, Reflective Black, Medium These are impressive laces. They are stiff, strong and can be pulled tight. I have been using two new pairs in mid and full size hiking boots that were a little large and I wanted them too fit snugly. They are working fine except for the length (longer than should be for the boots) and the bows can slip. I have been experimenting with tightening and using double knots. Each pair came with a different cord lock The metal one designed by Rhino so far seem too complicated to use and is time consuming setting it up. The plastic ones already broke. So, I like the laces and they are working the way I expected. I do need to master a better way to tie them.

1/5/15-After using these laces (two pairs on high and low hiking shoes), or trying to use these laces for 6 weeksI have given up and replaced them with waxed hiking laces. As noted, the two different style cord locks that were sent with each pair of laces didn't work, I then bought two other styles of cord locks, which were useless. As a result I had to continue to double knotting them, which prevented slippage and untying but due to the stiffness (like wires) I had to repeat the tying process several times, which was time consuming, and because of the stiffness of the laces, couldn't tie them tight-in fact that were always loose.

Basically, these laces will work for someone that is concerned about exposure to fire-I was not. I bought them because I try and support Kickstarter products and assumed that they would work. They did not for me. Over time the laces develop kinks, like wires and this memory remains. The result s very frustrating if you knot them, as I did.

I assume that they would work as intended with an appropriate cord lock, which I gather the inventor of the laces is trying to develop.

text_fidelity_a:
Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model) Britax has been making things for children for a very long time and it enjoys a strong reputation as a company that produces quality products. The high regard myself and others have for Britax was enough to convince me to obtain this bicycle seat and I have not regretted my decision.

I have two small girls, one of whom is still small enough to use a seat such as this. The weight limit is 40 pounds, so it is only going to work for children roughly four years of age or younger. My little one is still light enough and when she was first introduced, she took to this seat right away. She likes the adventurous feeling of riding on the back of the bicycle and I feel good knowing that she is safe and secure.

Looking at the specifics of this Britax bicycle seat, the seat is very sturdy in construction and it takes about 20 minutes from the box to the point where it is ready to use. It fits most all bicycles with 26 to 28 inch wheels, which would be just about every adult bicycle manufactured. It has a built in suspension for your child's comfort and this can be a great asset if the roads or sidewalks in your area are full of potholes and bumps. The headrest has nine position settings, the footrest has fifteen positions, and the harness locks securely in place, for maximum safety. The padding can be removed and is machine washable, for added convenience, and the product carries a limited two- year warranty.

Going for a spin with a child in a small seat behind you is quite an adventure and it does take getting used to. The added weight means you have to be more careful when you stop, when you start, and how you maneuver because you always have to be mindful of the child behind you and their safety. I admit that I was a little anxious when I used this at first, but my anxiety quickly faded when I started to ride. Once you get the hang of it, like anything, it gets easier. And it is very fun for the small child in the back who gets to enjoy the sites and the excitement of riding out in the open.

All things considered, I am hard pressed to find anything wrong with this bicycle seat and I recommend it for those with small children who like the adventure and fitness they receive from riding a bicycle. I would like to ride more, and perhaps this bicycle seat will encourage me to get more active. The seat is solid in construction, fairly easy to install, and made with safety in mind. It has all the earmarks of another quality Britax product and it earns a easy recommendation.

But this is my concern about the pack so far: First, out of the gate, the "clip" fastener that fastens the hood of the pack to the body is too small and will not lock in. That needs to be changed out and I need the company to send me a replacement part. I have already notified them about this.. we will see.

The other issue that I originally did not anticipate was going to be a big deal is there are very few pouches on the outside of the pack. The two diagonal zippered pouches on the front are not well designed for holding a lot of stuff. NOW perhaps that design was intentional to keep the weight distribution a certain way. I could see that.. But If you are looking for functionality and organization you pretty much will need to rely on individually bagging your items and arranging them INSIDE the pack. I have watched several packing videos and so I know that there is an art form for doing that .. I have a bit of ADHD and need to make sure I Have a system where i can find things easily. I am concerned that I wll not have enough pouches to keep things organized.. we will see. I know one suggestion is to put different "textures" of bags into the pack to help you find things by feel. Perhaps also have different tags (but that would put more weight in the pack). So I don't know. Not being a hard core hiker I can't tell if this will be the good starting backpack for my needs!. I just at least need to get that new clip for the pack ....

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

text_fidelity_a: OCOOPA Rechargeable Hand Warmers, 10000mAH Electric Handwarmer Winter Warm 15 Hours Portable Hands Heater for Men Women When I was a kid my dad used to hand me his hand warmer when we were outside during cold weather.  It was a "manual" kind - the interior had something like rock wool that was soaked in butane and lit and then the metal casing was slid inside a thick insulated bag and put in your pocket.  It could get rather hot!  I mention this because it brings back fond memories, but also to illustrate the difference in the "old fashioned" hand warmers and this one.  I love how easy this is to charge, even in my car, and the 3 levels of warmth depending on how cold it is and/or what you are doing.  I can put this in my pocket on low heat while I'm scraping the ice off my windshield and windows, then grab the warmer and let my fingers regain some feeling before trading the scraper for the shovel and shoveling the snow away from the car and off the sidewalk.  However many times I need to, I can stop shoveling and grab the warmer to keep my hands and fingers from going numb - that's what I appreciate having this handwarmer!  If you have kids that wait at the bus stop or have to walk to school even in winter, giving them a handwarmer might be just the thing to give them a "boost" of warmth while standing in the cold!
text_fidelity_b: OCOOPA Rechargeable Hand Warmers, 10000mAH Electric Handwarmer Winter Warm 15 Hours Portable Hands Heater for Men Women

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Colorado Buffaloes Can Cooler, 16

Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands I remember as a young man I used to be able to do 10 pull ups. 30+ years later, I tried to do a pull-up and couldn't even do one - not even half of one, actually. It's been 6 months, and I am still working on 2. Someone told me that this is because I'm not going through the whole pull-up motion often enough to build the muscles and that I should go to a gym and use a machine that gives you an assist so you can go through repetitions of the whole motion - over time, the assist is then reduced without reducing the number of repetitions. Well, I live too far from a gym - so I got these assist bands. And the first time I tried them after installation, I did 5 pull-ups - and could have done more! Starting tomorrow I will do 10 pull-ups and then reduce the number of straps over time.

The only downside to this solution is that if you don't have your pull-up bars installed high enough, you have to fiddle around with the strap length or put your knees in the stirrup instead of the feet. But that's not the bands' fault.
text_fidelity_b: Fitarc Pull Up Assist Bands,Pull Up Resistance Bands for Chin Up,Adjustable Pullup Bands

Out of the box...I went with the Pro Beetle because it stated it got more range for my buck and I wanted the best one. So this review is for the more pricey pro model. So... to start off. I bought the green one. Let me tell you there is nothing really green about it. I will contact the company later to inquire why my bike straight up looks powder blue no matter what lighting it's in. They could really afford to change that color to seafood if anything. Nit a big deal but haf I known I'd have opted for pink or white since it hardly looks even a smidgen green.
Anyway. Set up wad meh. Everything ran smoothly till the last screw. The threads of the screw got damaged as I tightened the last bold to the handlebar area. Sadly there is no way to remove it so it sticks there not fully in. Not a big deal but could have used better metal for them screws.
It wad at a 60 percent charge out of the box so I let it it to 80 and took her out for a 2 mile spin. I came back and the battery life was at 66. Not too bad but I'll be pushing that battery life to the limit once I'm at a full charge and report back.

The ride. Not terrible at all. I wad easily reaching the max speed of 15 and felt a few spots of drag going on small inclines. Not too bad though. If anything I dropped speed by a few knots.

The app was a pain to figure out but I realized why some folks are not getting their ride history is because you must have your phones Bluetooth and location set to on. Battery hogs however. But if they're not on you won't get a reading. So if you want that feature turn them on...on your phone ! Easy fix.

The cons... the one con so far was a lack of instructions on how to turn the front light on. Mine didn't turn on so I am not are how to activate it? Maybe it comes on at night with a sensor. I don't know.

The other con was that I wish the bike came with mirrors. I switch lanes and didn't like having to turn to look behind me. I purchased some mirrors but the company could have easily added then considering how pricey this bike is.
I scooted around with my son which added a bit more weight. Battery life is effected by your weight. I weigh under 220 but with my son with me I'm sure we maxed it. He weighs 50. The battery drained by a few more knots but hardly.
Update... I wad able to add my own wicker basket that i found here on Amazon. Way cheaper than the teeny one they try to sell separately. The one draw back is it covered the light a little. Doesn't matter much to me though because I don't ride at night and I can't figure out how to turn it on anyway. Haha.
More to come....
So far I love the bike. The look is fun and I'll use it mostly for local commute.

The one other con wad the foot pedal area where your feet got mine won't lock tight Soni contacted the company and will update how well customer service gets this resolved

Update... the company is flat pit refusing to resolve the issue with the foot pedal not sitting flush or locking proper. Their solution is to send the entire bike back instead of just sending me a foot rest that is not a defect. Don't buy from this company. This entire process has been a nightmare. It's been over a week now woth back and forth troubleshooting over a piece of plastic that won't cost but 10.00
Because of this I'll probably be setting up a return with refund and buy another bike. The battery life is crap..said up to 25 miles or something on the pro. I'm lucky I get 5 on a full charge. Trash
Update 3.... got even worse. Customer service is terrible. I simply needed a new foot rest because mine is defective. Instead of sending the part they want me to return it for a replacement. The entire bike! Hogwash! There is no return for replacement and after the sale the price went up by 249.00 so they basically want me to return it and pay an additional 249.00 for a new one. This is disgusting.
Besides that... took it on a 2 mile run today and the battery went from 100 to 60. I guess I'll just be returning it and buying a whole new model because this pro model definitely will not get you a 25 mile range at all. Not even close. It is sooo slow going up small hills too. I'm sad I have to return it but at this point ots for the best. Terrible customer service. Clearly no warranty on defective parts ...don't waste your time with it. If the pro model is this terrible I cannot even imagine how bad the regular one is
Update November 10th... 10 days after returning still no refund. Amazon said it can take 30 days for a refund even though they got the item I'm being billed. I had to dispute the charges. Hopefully amazon moves faster now because this is unacceptable!
Never again with an oaki product
Update... do nit buy and return. I had to open a dispute because Amazon wanted me to wait 30 days to see my refund. I wad already being billed so I had no options and disputed with my card. I charged 550.88 to ny card and another 100.00 was an amazon giftcard. Amazon is refusing to refund the guftcard because a rep said I damaged the item. This is a filthy lie and the reason it was returned was because it was damaged. I'm not sure if the seller is telling lies or what but I am out a guftcard of100$ because Amazon says giftcards are non refundable..I have contacted the BBB and attorney General and next will be news 12. This has been the most disgusting transaction ever. Avoid this bike like the plague. It's garbage. You dont even get 6 Mike's out of it and the foot rest is defective

Update... took approximately 3 months to get a full refund and fighting with Amazon. Apparently the seller of this bike lied and said I damaged the bike. Disgusting. Wouldn't even answer basic question...why did you LIE? I did get a refund but ONLY because I disputed with my card and got the attorney General to force up the money. I purchased the pro model and see they still lie in advertising. Months and months later this gross company KNOWS the pro model does not and never will get 30 miles per charge. More like 7. If you're lucky. I hope this company folds and i pray this review helps buyers make the proper decision to AVOID it. I suggest a beautiful eleteic scooter from SOHO once I got my refund I bought from them and it's been fabulous.
text_fidelity_b: OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires

text_fidelity_a:
Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case I should have listened to the other 2 reviewers. I am beyond disappointed in the condition of this item. First of all, the fact that all the pieces were separate would not have been an issue IF the items were packed properly. The piece of sod was thrown haphazardly into a very thin plastic bag that was completely wide open and not secured closed at all. There is almost as much dirt and grass in the bottom of the bag as there is on the piece of sod. I'm surprised that there isn't dirt and grass all over the box it was thrown into as well. Worst of all, the sod is absolutely NOTHING like the picture. it is a 3 inch round piece of mostly dirt, that is not a rich dark brown as pictured, but a dried-out, tan-colored crumbling mess. And, the grass is long, sparse and a mix of pale green, yellow and brown. Not sure what the freeze-drying process is supposed to do, but the grass and dirt are so dry that you can't even breathe near it without pieces of grass and dirt falling off. What a mess! AND it smells pretty nasty too.

The letter of authenticity is trash (or at least it is to Steiner). It was thrown into the box along with the packing materials, without an envelope or any other protection. From being jostled around inside the shipping box, it is now crumpled and torn in at least three places along the side. Granted, it is a thicker-weight paper, but an envelope would have been nice (especially for the price). The letter says that the sod was removed on March 14, 2009 and that it is "unconditionally guaranteed" - whatever that means. It's difficult to tell if the signature of "Brandon Steiner" is signed in ink or a copy. I don't want to damage the signature trying to figure it out.

The case is actually a baseball case and comes in a "single baseball glass case" box. When I first opened the shipping box, I thought I'd been sent the wrong item. The case IS made of glass, not acrylic, and supposedly has a cherry wood base. It also is not nearly as nice as the picture depicts. The wood is dry and dull and the joints are roughly glued together and uneven. Unlike one of the other reviewers (and the description), I did not receive a separate sticker to apply to the base. It actually has a metal plaque already attached. The problem is, the only words that are legible are "Yankee Stadium Artifact." There are three full lines of smaller writing below that but it is completely unreadable. I can't tell if the words got scratched off or if it was improperly printed on the plate to begin with. I cannot read what it says at all.

I'm not familiar with these types of cases, but there is nothing that holds the grass in place. The bottom is a slick mirror, and the slightest movement causes the sod to slide around inside the case, leaving dirt and debris all over the bottom. Unless its kept perfectly still, it will probably fall apart completely into a big mess in no time. My biggest regret is that I did not purchase this from Amazon. I paid only $59 from another source who is not nearly as easy to deal with. Although, I don't think it would have made a difference in the quality of the product or awful packaging, because this item ships directly from Steiner sports anyway.

I've posted over 80 product reviews on Amazon. This is the first time I've ever felt the need to post pictures or video. This item is so pathetic - you really have to see it to believe it, so I am going to post something tomorrow. I just wanted to post my review ASAP so that anyone considering buying this as a last-minute Christmas gift is forewarned. I initially felt too embarrassed to give this as a gift, but now I think the recipient might appreciate the "tragic humor" of this item. It would make a good conversation piece for sure! I will let him decide if he wants to return it for something else, or keep it as something to show to his friends and laugh about.
text_fidelity_b: Steiner Sports MLB New York Yankees Authentic Yankee Stadium "Freeze Dried Grass" Sod w/ Glass Display Case

Crankbrothers Doubleshot Hybrid Bike Pedal - Flat/Clipped-In City Bicycle Pedal, Premium Bearings and Seals I've been using Crank Brothers eggbeater pedals for many years. I got these doubleshot pedals for my commuter bike. Really nice to have the option to use either flat shoes or cleated shoes on the same pedals. The pedals are big enough that the flat side is very stable and flipping to the side you want is easy. The cleated side is easy enough to click in and out. It feels a little different from the eggbeater pedals, but I got used to that quickly. I use the same shoes/cleats that I use with the eggbeater pedals with no problems. A new set of Crank Brothers cleats is included with the pedals for people that are new to Crank Brothers.

I'm using the cheapest 1-series version of these pedals. The 2-series has more durable bearings, which frequent users will probably want. The 3-series has the improved bearings as well as adjustable studs on the flat side of the pedal. Use a small hex wrench to raise or lower the stud height. Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick I’ve had my eye on another brand for awhile, but wasn’t sure - a single ring is around $25 - being concerned the silicone wouldn’t work, feel good, or have any give. My ring finger tapers and can go up and down during the day, so metal rings can go from loose to tight. Would this kind work? While not metal pricing, I still didn’t want to pay for another ring to sit in the drawer.

I am thrilled with these rings.

First, I got two sets: I literally fell on the line between the two sizes so figured it would be smarter than risking it. My ring finger is the smaller of the two, but I still get use of the larger set on other fingers. Usually not at the same time - looks a little goofy.

Second, I wasn’t sure on the grip - would they work on my tapered finger and would they have any give. Yes to both. In fact the only time I have an “issue” with being loose is washing my hands. I have to watch a bit, holding fingers tight, but otherwise the rings both stay snug and on, as well as give a little when humidity expands them. I love the fit, the size and look on my finger, and that little give.

Third, Yes, I keep them on when washing my hands, but I do take the ring off to dry it as well. Otherwise it will retain moisture - it does get annoying and loosens the fit. I have worn them to shower, but now keep it off, just in case.

Forth, working out and doing things with them on is a breeze. I lift weights (with/without gloves) play pickle ball, do chores, you name it, and the rings hold up. There is no issue and I don’t have to worry about damaging, bending, or otherwise having any problems.

Fifth, The Colors... Interesting. Some I love and look really nice on their own and on my hand. Some I just don’t like. It’s a personal taste thing, but some look cartoonish or goofy. Overall, it’s a personal thing, so have some fun. I was surprised I liked the look of the bright blue, red (thought I’d hate it), and tie dye.

Sixth, there is a slight difference between the cuts of these two sets I got. I include image to show: one is rounded, the other sharp cut. Not sure you can tell from product page the difference - I didn’t until they arrived.

These are some great rings for the price and I do like that I got different sizes. I do wear the larger ones on other fingers from time to time, but I love that I can now wear a wedding ring and not worry. (* Same review given for the other set in order to stay consistent with my experience)
text_fidelity_b: Elimoons Silicone Wedding Ring for Men - 10 Rings&Singles Silicone Rubber Wedding Bands- 8.7 mm Wide - 2.5mm Thick

Also: Important information is left out of the description in that once the can is opened it will only keep for 7 days. That's fine if you plan to eat a lot of eggs for the next week, but really, I think this is important enough to mention.

I do want to emphasize the fact that the flavor is great. Actually, these eggs tasted much better than the breakfast burrito I had from Jack In The Box earlier in the week. text_fidelity_a:
MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.
text_fidelity_b: MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag

He always wears a work shirt. This did not allow other patrons to see it. So the flag idea came into mind. The Hawkeyes car flag was the perfect size and of course looked cool. Right now there are two Hawkeye flags flying in Japan and when asked where I'm from we can point to the flag. It serves the Bar owners because it gives them and others a sense they are valued. It serves me because when I pronounce Iowa they spell it out as Aiowaa.
The Flags are of higher quality than I was expecting. It is not a single fabric with print on both sides. It was two fabrics sewn together or folded over and sewn. text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Incline Treadmill I've owned several lower end treadmills over the past 20+ years, but the T-4400 is my first Sunny, and it's the best of the under-$500 treadmills I've owned. The description and videos are accurate; I chose it partly because I wanted a treadmill that offered a no-incline option and an incline option and some kind of shock absorption, and this has both. And it's worth mentioning that the treadmill was very well packaged to avoid damage in shipping.

Since I walk or speed walk on treadmills, the first and to me most important thing about the Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Treadmill T4400 is that doesn't slow down or bog down when I'm walking on it. The other treadmills I've owned dragged when you walked - they'd slow down and speed up, and you can hear their motors struggling. Every one was properly oiled before use, and the tension was correct, so I guess they had weaker motor or the motors had less torque. The Sunny doesn't have this issue, and we did oil it first as per instructions.

I like the way it opens slowly so I don't have to do something keep it from slamming to the floor, potentially damaging the floor or the treadmill. A big surprise is that the heart rate monitor on mine is accurate - I tested it wearing a pulse oximeter while holding the heart rate monitor at the same time, and they both read the exact same number. I like the speed up and slow down buttons on the arms, but I did hit the speed up button a couple times when I meant to slow down.

Some people complain that the arms are too low. Well, I'm only 5' 3 1/2, and they were comfortable for me. They could be low for taller people, but I found them just right.

One thing that is probably not going to be accurate for most people is the calorie count. Unlike most machines that overcount, this under-counts the calories dramatically for me. That's okay - I have apps and a heart rate monitor. I have no idea if the distance calculated is correct, but for me, that's not an issue.

Instead of a treadmill mat, we put pieces of dense ethylene vinyl acetate foam sheets - fairly thick sheets - under each foot, and it made the treadmill quieter and reduced the impact of walking on it just a little.

Two last things. First, I've owned other Sunny products, and I also called them with questions about this treadmill. Both their phone and email support have been friendly and helpful. Also my husband bought this for me with his Amazon account, which is why it's not showing as a verified purchase.

I wasn't expecting much out of this Sunny Health & Fitness T4400, which is why I am so impressed. Many treadmills claim to have 0% incline, but in reality they have an incline - the Sunny is 0% or so close that I can't tell, and for someone in average condition, the higher incline is helpful. The heart rate monitor is accurate, the motor doesn't bog down when walking fast, slow, with or without an incline, and the display is easy to read. The shock absorbers aren't as good as a Sole, but for less than a quarter of the price, they do help and you can put a rubber mat under it to absorb a bit more impact. I'm so happy with this that when it comes time to upgrade, I'll most likely get another Sunny.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Incline Treadmill

Dechunxian Best Collapsible Cup Foldable Silicone Sports Water Bottle Camping Canteens 550ml (Blue) This has to be one of the oddest water bottles I've come across. It's made of silicon, which means it's all squishy and soft to the touch. I had my doubts when I first took it out of the package, but it really works well and offers benefits that I don't have with my other bottles.

The main benefit is that you can roll the bottle up into a pretty tight bundle. It comes with a silicon band (about the size of a typical rubber band) to hold the bottle when it's folded. That feature is great for traveling - when you're done with the water, just fold up the bottle and tuck it away. It will easily fit into a pocket when folded.

The soft silicone also has a benefit when the bottle is filled. I usually carry a metal water bottle in my messenger bag, and have received a poke in the ribs on more than one occasion from the bottle shifting around. This silicon is much nicer - no hard edges to poke me in the ribs. It also has a carabineer clip on the top so it can be clipped onto a bag, backpack or belt.

Despite the soft feel, this is pretty durable. I have not had any problems with it tearing or splitting, and I'm not all that gentle on my water bottles. The silicon is thick enough that I'm confident it will stand up to a good amount of use. It has a flip-top cover that is easy to open one-handed. Since it's silicon, you can squeeze the bottle and have the water shoot out rather than have to tilt the bottle back to take a drink. It's a nice feature to have when you're using this while exercising.

The only downside to the silicon is that it's not the best choice for use in a car cup holder. The sides will bend in, making it less than ideal in terms of stability. It does stand on its own when filled, but can be a bit bendy when it's partially filled. This is much more of an on-the-go type of bottle.

It feels rather odd, doesn't look like a bottle at all when you get it folded up, but it works extremely well as an easy way to take water along without having to deal with the size and weight of a metal bottle, or the fixed shape of a plastic bottle. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Dechunxian Best Collapsible Cup Foldable Silicone Sports Water Bottle Camping Canteens 550ml (Blue)

United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife I went through and read the good and the bad reviews. Taking all that into account and knowing what I know about knives, which as a retired chef is quite a bit, I decided to take a chance on this one.

First, even after reading the numerous reviews and manufacturer's info, I was astounded by the length of this knife. It is LONG. Not only is this knife long, it's heavy.

Second, as many noted, the knife blade wasn't all that sharp when received. Again, noting my background as a retired chef, taking care of knives and bringing them from the land of the dead to an item with a wonderfully usuable blade isn't all that difficult providing you've the equipment to do so.

I honed the knife using the medium grit on my tri-stone about 10 minutes then moved to the fine grit stone. That put a good edge on it. While watching Firefly (http://www.amazon.com/Firefly-Complete-Blu-ray-Nathan-Fillion/dp/B001EN71CW/ref=sr_1_3?s=movies-tv&ie=UTF8&qid=1363822981&sr=1-3&keywords=firefly), I pulled out the tri-stone again and continued with the medium to fine grit honing getting an even better blade on it.

The scabbard is appropriate for the knife. That, to me, says a lot. There's a lot of knife, there's a lot of scabbard. One other reviewer succinctly defined the contents of the pockets on the scabbard. I needn't do the same. Nor shall I wax about which pieces are good and which aren't. Everybody's entitled to their own opinions about that. That said, I'm keeping "most" of the prepackaged stuff there. I'm sure over the course of a few trips I'll update, tweak and tune what I want, but for the time being, it all stays.

I'm very satisifed with this knife. I know while I'm backpacking, hiking or camping I'll keep it close at hand. My son's got HIS knife, Whetstone Usa Full Tang Stainless Steel Jungle Survival Knife, (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003U7SC6O/ref=oh_details_o06_s00_i01?ie=UTF8&psc=1), I've got mine.

Happy honing.
text_fidelity_b: United Cutlery Bushmaster Survival Knife

KIZEN Solar Lantern - Collapsible LED Camping Lantern - Rechargeable Solar - USB Portable Lamp and Phone Charger for Emergency, Power Outage, Hurricane - Tent Lights, Hiking, Backpacking Gear, Yellow I ordered two lanterns. Received them quickly. After opening found that one was missing everything from inside the box except the lantern itself. No charging cord, no bubble wrap…
The other one came with everything in the box. I am not going to return because I have a lot of cords in my house, but still disappointed. It tells me
that there is a luck of quality check before shipping. And no, I don’t think it’s amazon fault, because box itself is not damaged. It’s whoever was packing products inside those boxes.
As to performance, I turned them
both on, they work as a flashing or as a lantern. Lighter and dimmer options both work. As to the SOS signal, both are blinking just steady without longer-shorter breaks. Basically they are sending just SSSSS and not SOS like it should be, so no, it’s not a SOS, it’s just blinking with no information in it. It is what it is. I got them not for that, but to use as a lantern in our tent. Can’t speak about longevity yet and for how long fully charged battery would last. We will see. Three starts for today for missing real SOS and missing cord and wrap on one of them.
text_fidelity_b: KIZEN Solar Lantern - Collapsible LED Camping Lantern - Rechargeable Solar - USB Portable Lamp and Phone Charger for Emergency, Power Outage, Hurricane - Tent Lights, Hiking, Backpacking Gear, Yellow

Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm) I just received this from my wife as a Christmas gift. I have gone on 3 rides ranging from 20-60 miles and this helmet is great. A few months ago I went into my favorite local bike shop asking about helmets because I seem to have an unusually large head......yea, a mellon head. Most of the helmets I've tried were too small, too heavy, straps ran weird and uncomfortable, or just plain SQUARE. The Lasor O2 fit like no other helmet I've ever tried. This summer I started useing a "halo" sweat band and I have no problem with the fit, even with my huge mellon head. The unique helmet features a "adjustment dial" that will fine tune the fit to your head with laser percision. This helmet is much lighter than my old Bell I used to wear. You might not notice this on a 10-20 mile ride but if you ride any longer distances you will feel it. During the summer months, I live in Michigan, I try to do one century a month and ...BOY, I can hardly wait to do my first one this year. Another very important feature about this helmet is ....IT LOOKS COOL!! Even my niehbor who likes to make fun of cyclists because of there "pointy hats" said this one looks cool.

Don't look at another helmet. This is the best I've EVER worn. If you cycle a lot, don't hesitate. It's a bit more money but for the serious cyclist it's worth every penny. I try to ride at least 100 mile a week during the good months. If you ride simply with a family or short distances you might want to concider a cheaper model.....unless you have a big fat mellon head like me.
text_fidelity_b: Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm)

60 Lumen Theft Proof Rear Bike Light For Bicycle Commuters - Super Bright USB Rechargeable LED Rear Bicycle Light w/ Lifetime Anti Theft Guarantee This is a sturdy light with a metal housing and a very bright tail light. Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

text_fidelity_a:
SureFire Titan Ultra-Compact LED Keychain Light Series BACKGROUND:
I am a big fan of Surefire products, and I have had a LOT of flashlights over the last 40 years.
I try to purchase products that are "made in America" whenever possible, even when they cost substantially more.
I have had a Fenix LD02 single AAA battery flashlight (under $35 at REI) for about one year now.
I ordered this Surefire, because it appeared to be about 3 times brighter, and about the same size, as my Fenix.

MY REVIEW:
1). Like many other reviewers, I have NO IDEA why they decided to make this out of brass. It feels three times as heavy as my aluminum Fenix LD02. That was just a very odd decision. Its like we went back in time to some point before the Bronze age...oh well...
2). In order to turn this on and off and to select the various brightness levels, you have to twist the cap on and off relatively slowly. It always resets to the lowest setting.
Here again, the $35 Fenix wins out--it has a button switch on the tailcap.
3). It is a little bigger than the Fenix, for unknown reasons.
4). Apparently, to achieve the 300 lumen setting, you need to use the included Eneloop Pro rechargeable battery (buy your own charger).
5). On the highest setting, the Surefire beam is noticeably brighter and wider than the Fenix LD02.

CONCLUSION:
If I had to do it again, I would have just stuck with my smaller, lighter, and easier to operate Fenix LD02 that (to me) appears to be about 50% as bright on the highest setting.
text_fidelity_b: SureFire Titan Ultra-Compact LED Keychain Light Series

text_fidelity_a: Thule T2 Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack (1.25"), Black We were so excited to get our new bike rack, but have been really disappointed. I followed all the guidelines and made sure this was the correct rack for my Subaru XV, and the right size for our dealer installed tow package.  First issue is that the safety latch doesn't fit right on the tow hitch. We were able to work around the issue and that hasn't been a problem.  We took the car on a 400 mile round trip road trip on highway and it did great.... the problem started last month. My husband got a new mountain bike with 29 in tires. We were driving maybe 5 miles from our house on a bumpy dirt road and despite being locked down really well, the bike bounced off and got dragged. He was NOT happy.  He thought maybe it was user error or he didn't do something right, and he went out again, this time putting his 27" tire bike on the back and making sure everything was locked down, but unfortunately the same thing happened on the super bumpy road. The bike got bumped off. So now we are trying to figure out what to do with our really expensive bike rack that is great on highway, but sadly, despite Thule being such a respectable name, has almost resulted in destroying two VERY expensive mountain bikes. We are very upset with our product and do not recommend it to anyone.  DO NOT BUY!!!!
text_fidelity_b: Thule T2 Pro XT 2 Hitch Bike Rack (1.25"), Black

If I had to store a couple traditional aluminum frame bikes, I would be concerned at the stand collapsing due to its stability. As an enhancement, it would be nice to have adjustable height between the two bikes.

Second, the bike frame holders are not necessarily thick enough. It works fine for a road bike, but triathlon or mountain bikes would need a cross bar to comfortably fit. I think it would be nice to have slightly lengthier frame holder, especially since the footprint is already there.

On the plus side, assembly is simple. Especially if you already have a socket set handy.

Tennis Headbands for Men, Sweat Bands Headbands Men(3 Pack) for Yoga Gym Running Cycling Basketball Workout Accessories Stretchy Moisture Wicking Sweat Band for Women… UPDATE: I’ve been able to get back to working out and wearing these headbands while lifting weights, hitting a heavy bag, and on walks. In all cases they work out great and do as intended. I’ve been keeping the sweat out of my eyes and staying comfortable. Please read the rest of the review where I address why I still can’t give them 5 stars.

First, I grabbed these Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) because I tend to seat a lot when working out and am tired of the sweat dripping down my face and into my eyes. I thought they looked cool.

I have debated on 4 or 5 stars, which I address below.

1. So, they do look as cool in person. My wife is not a big fan of headbands - thinks they look weird - but she saw them and immediately said they looked great. I agree. I like the solid black, but I equally like the patterns. Happy to wear them from that standpoint. The material feel nice. I find them comfortable on. To this point I think they are 5 stars.

NOTE: I strained my knee badly and have been off it for a week and told I need to give it several more days. therefore, I have not been able to wear them during a workout yet. I will come back and update IF they are anything but great. To this point I can only give 4 stars, with 5 a possibility.

2. Under Armour??? I am a big UA fan with a lot of UA gear. The title on the product page caught my attention, but mainly because 1. I love UA and 2. I did not see any UA logos on the product page. The headbands themselves do not have the UA logo. So I am confused as to why they are allowed to use the Under Armour brand name when as far as I can tell, they are nothing of the kind. To this point, I have to give them 4 stars. Without them being actual Under Armour they are still a fine product, but I am not okay with using the brand name when from everything I can tell, these are not made by nor sold by UA. My wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.

3. The sizing is mostly the same, but... I found that the solid and the blue pattern are the same size. I have a larger head (usually a baseball hat L-XL), but in this case while they fit spot on, the black pattern was slightly larger. Not working out, merely having them all, it was fine, but I will be curious if they all stay on the same. A smaller ahed might have an issue with the one, but I “think” smaller heads would be okay with the two. To this point I decide to go with a 4 star, as they are not consistent and I do expect them to be.

4. I cannot speak to their ability to keep the sweat off. My injury happened shortly after I ordered these and before they arrived, so that’s kept me from using them for their intended purpose. So right now I can only give them a 4 star rating. But to be fair, even if they come back 100% as expected, I am still bothered enough by the use of the Under Armour name - a brand name I do use often - on the product page when nothing on the actual product indicates they are UA - such as the UA logo. Therefore, for me, I could still not give these a full 5 star rating as I consider this action deceptive. This is a personal opinion and is mentioned here so as to fully explain why I would still consider this a 4 star product.

In the end I do - so far - like these headbands and think I’ll get some good use out of them. But Would rather they not use a brand name to promote them. When you literally write - Tennis Headbands for Men, Under Armour Headbands Men(3 Pack) as the title of the product then I expect they would be an Under Armour product and again, I cannot find any evidence of this being the case on the actual headbands. As stated above, my wife and I have both looked at all 3 headbands separately and together - there is NO Under Armour logo or labeling.
text_fidelity_b: Tennis Headbands for Men, Sweat Bands Headbands Men(3 Pack) for Yoga Gym Running Cycling Basketball Workout Accessories Stretchy Moisture Wicking Sweat Band for Women…

I didn't even want to try another one, but to get my partner to agree to go camping I had to supply an air mattress so I went with the one with the highest rating within my budget and waited to be disappointed. Imagine my surprise. You can charge the pump from your vehicle (no batteries! which was great because they didn't even cross my mind) or from a regular outlet. The pump is noisy but not unusually so, and the mattress inflated pretty darn quick. It was ample for 2 large people and 2 small dogs. Best of all, incredibly, it didn't deflate overnight! I did "top it off" a bit for the 3rd night but over-all it was full and comfy, survived excited dogs and 40 degree weather, the pump has a reverse so you can deflate it really fast, and somehow, someway, it actually all fit back easily into the box it came in so we can keep it safe for next time. It wasn't even overpoweringly stinky like plastic usually is (we still aired it out of course, how stinky is too stinky being quite subjective but neither of us was bothered).  If someone asked me to recommend an air mattress, I would gleefully direct them to this one.

I bought it to move our Sunfish sailboat and Dyer Dink dinghy. These are both too heavy and awkward to launch without a dolly.

text_fidelity_a: Razor A4 Kick Scooter OK, so I had to have one of these contraptions.  Both my kids had Zootrs for Eco Challenges and tootling around Chicago but I was going to use mine for exercise.  Good choice since cleaning out a clogged sewer ranks above running and biking on my list of druthers. My initial considerations were finding one for an adult weighing more than 90 pounds and costing less than $300.  This seemed to be about the only one.  Had just purchased a motorized Razor (300) for my daughter to ride back and forth from the train station and was very impressed with its quality. However, the size and weight of my new Razor A4 kick scooter surprised me. It's a trick scooter and one should seriously consider its handlebar warning stating "this object moves when in use. Take safety precautions."  OK, I just turned 65 and I'm probably not in the target demographic group, but I'm getting pretty good on it and look less like an idiot every day.  Caution though because the standing area is short and narrow and I have big feet so I tend to switch legs a lot while using the opposing leg for propulsion.  The wheels are tiny and buck whenever they hit a piece of gravel or a twig.  The "trick" is avoiding obstacles in the street.  Have fun.  It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks.  I'm going to borrow one of my kids' Zootrs though and save the Razor A4 for exhibition!
text_fidelity_b: Razor A4 Kick Scooter
